newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SUEZ NO PLAN TO DITCH SGB HOLDING STRUCTURE - SGB.
newsitem.headline: SUEZ NO PLAN TO DITCH SGB HOLDING STRUCTURE - SGB.

text.p: French Compagnie de Suez has no plan to drop Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) as an intermediate holding company for its Belgian assets, SGB said on Thursday.
"The Suez-SGB relation is working well, and the cost of the Belgian holding structure is minimal," SGB chairman of the board Etienne Davingon told Reuters in an interview.
The 175-year old Belgian holding company has often been criticised for being an unneccessary vehicle between Suez and its extensive Belgian assets.
Suez holds 62 percent of SGB following an acrimonious takeover battle with Italian financier Carlo de Benedetti in 1988.
"The essential part of SGB's portfolio is managed from Belgium, this is where most of our business activities are," Davignon said.

He said that SGB acquisition of an additional 25 percent stake in utility holding company Tractebel SA last year -- preventing it from falling in foreign hands -- proved the use of an active Belgian shareholder structure.
"We have not yet found a legal instrument which would improve our present situation," Davignon said.
Current Suez chief Gerard Mestrallet spent several years in Belgium as chief executive officer of SGB before heading back to Paris in 1995.
